entry.title: Inside Julianne Moore’s Rooftop NYC Home | Open Door | Architectural Digest

media:group.media:title: Inside Julianne Moore’s Rooftop NYC Home | Open Door | Architectural Digest
media:group.media:description:
Julianne Moore welcomes AD into her New York City home, designed with architect Oliver Freundlich. The Oscar-winning actor has filled her 1920s rooftop apartment with art, vintage furniture, and collectible design pieces, including works by George Nakashima and Isamu Noguchi. From her beautiful rooftop terrace, working fireplace, and marble bathroom, Julianne’s home is a calming oasis in the midst of the big city.

entry.title: Inside a Gilded Age Mansion Designed to Hide Its Servants | Inside History | Architectural Digest

media:group.media:title: Inside a Gilded Age Mansion Designed to Hide Its Servants | Inside History | Architectural Digest
media:group.media:description:
Architectural Digest explores The Elms, a spectacular 60,000-square-foot Gilded Age mansion in Newport, Rhode Island. Built in 1901 for Edward and Herminie Berwind, this lavish summer home features imported marble, gilt bronze, historic artwork, and architecture designed to conceal the labor behind its luxury. Discover hidden servant staircases, secret passageways, a two-story butler’s pantry, concealed living quarters, and an underground coal tunnel that kept this extraordinary mansion running seamlessly behind the scenes.
